rv.q: Anna Francolini as the dumped Callas makes the most of her over the top role as a tragic Cassandra-like figure invoking the Greek gods to bring down a curse on her wayward lover. Lydia Leonard purrs prettily as the mercenary trophy wife Jacquie with a hard to place accent, while Liz Crowther has a fine cameo as the poignant mother figure Eleni.
This is a ridiculous play that treats a delusional tycoon as if a figure of epic grandeur.
The ever-magnificent Robert Lindsay gives a gripping performance as the despotic Onassis with a fearsome, manic gleam raging behind the tortoiseshell glasses.
